context: A uni student interviews a retired executive about associations
purpose: Teach: 入会/申し出/任命/協同/商法/商工/労使/単行本

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間をいただきありがとうございます。退職後に商工会議所の役員に任命されたと伺いましたが、入会のきっかけは何でしたか。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. I heard you were appointed as an officer of the Chamber of Commerce after retirement—what led you to join?
lines.style: Polite, slightly nervous student opening a formal interview.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: いやいや、こちらこそ。実はね、現役時代の同僚から「ぜひ入会してほしい」という申し出があったんだよ。断る理由もなかったしね。
lines.en: No, no, the pleasure is mine. Actually, a former colleague from my working days made an offer saying he really wanted me to join. I had no reason to refuse.
lines.style: Warm, relaxed elder reminiscing with a soft chuckle.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど。商工会議所のほかにも、協同組合のような団体に関わっていらっしゃるんですか。
lines.en: I see. Besides the Chamber of Commerce, are you also involved with organizations like cooperative associations?
lines.style: Curious follow-up, leaning forward with notebook ready and pen poised.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ああ、地元の協同組合の顧問もしているよ。中小企業を支える仕組みは、若い君たちにこそ知ってほしいねえ。
lines.en: Ah, yes, I also serve as an advisor for the local cooperative association. I'd really like young people like you to learn about systems that support small businesses.
lines.style: Gently encouraging, almost grandfatherly tone, personal cadence that sets them apart

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: ありがとうございます。大学の授業で商法を学んでいるのですが、労使関係についてはあまり触れられなくて。実務ではどうでしたか。
lines.en: Thank you. I've been studying commercial law in my university classes, but we don't cover labor-management relations much. How was it in actual practice?
lines.style: Earnest student steering toward academic curiosity.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 教科書ではきれいに書かれているけれど、労使の交渉は本当に泥臭いものだったよ。毎晩、夜遅くまで話し合ったこともあった。
lines.en: It's written neatly in textbooks, but labor-management negotiations were truly gritty work. There were nights we talked until very late.
lines.style: Reflective, voice lowering with the weight of memory.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 貴重なお話ですね。そのご経験を単行本にまとめるご予定はないんですか。ぜひ読んでみたいです。
lines.en: What a valuable story. Do you have any plans to compile your experiences into a book? I'd really love to read it.
lines.style: Genuine enthusiasm, eyes brightening at the idea.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: はは、出版社からも声はかかったんだがね、自分の話を単行本にするのは、なんだか照れくさくてさ。でも、君のような学生がいるなら、考え直してみようかな。
lines.en: Haha, a publisher did approach me, but turning my own story into a book feels a bit embarrassing. Still, if there are students like you, maybe I'll reconsider.
lines.style: Bashful but pleased, laughing softly at himself.
